provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft; host source restrictions and execution verification

draft_notes.explanation:
Original mechanism, before any D4 map:
- Seeds are sorted by row.
- Each seed paints its full row.
- The left and right border columns are split into bands. Each border cell takes the colour of the nearest seed by row. When a cell is exactly between two seeds, it goes to the upper seed: the generator gives the upper band rows through floor((p+q)/2).
- Row 0 takes the topmost seed's colour and the last row takes the bottommost seed's colour.

How the factory adapts it to the visible grid:
- It tracks where the original 'up' direction ends up. A row reversal does not change it, and each clockwise turn maps up to right, then down, then left.
- If 'up' stays vertical (d4%4 in {0,2}), seeds are sorted by row. Each seed paints a full row, bands go on the left/right columns, and the caps are the top and bottom rows.
- Otherwise seeds are sorted by column. Each seed paints a full column, bands go on the top/bottom rows, and the caps are the leftmost and rightmost columns.
- Tie breaking is the only direction-sensitive part. A tie goes to the lower-index seed when 'up' maps to up or left (k=0 or 3), and to the higher-index seed when it maps to down or right (k=1 or 2).
- The caps use the minimum-index and maximum-index seed colours. This rule is the same in every orientation.
- The background constant is palette[0]. Seed colours are read from the pixels, so no colour permutation is needed.
draft_notes.limitations:
- The background is assumed to be palette[0], which is what the generator always uses for the blank canvas.
- Seeds are assumed to occupy distinct lines along the seed axis. The generator guarantees this with distinct rows at least 2 apart; if two seeds did share a line, the code would still run but the result would be arbitrary.
- Rectangular grids are handled generically even though the generator only produces 15x15.
- No fixture contradicts the rule. All four train pairs and the test pair match the formula floor((p+q)/2), ties upward.
- I have not run any tests on this factory.
